newsitem.title: ITALY: Strong dollar not seen a worry for Italy - Micheli.
newsitem.headline: Strong dollar not seen a worry for Italy - Micheli.

text.p: The dollar's current strength against the lira is not for the moment a worry for Italian inflation, cabinet undersecretary Enrico Micheli said.

Asked by reporters about eventual inflationary effects of the strong dollar, which on Monday touched a 12-year high above 1,800 against the lira, Micheli said "over the long term perhaps it's possible but in the current Italian situation I really don't think so."
Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a newspaper interview on Tuesday that a dollar at 1,800 lire did not help Italy but did not pose an inflationary threat.
Micheli also denied Italian press reports of a one-off "tax for Italy". Italians this year have been hit by a so-called Eurotax on incomes to help Italy reach EMU goals.
"Reading about this supertax this morning I was very surprised because truly it's never been discussed," he said.
The Finance Ministry later put out a statement "categorically" denying that any new taxes or extraordinary contributions were being studied, calling the speculation "pure fantasy."

Some newspapers said the government could be thinking of increasing current workers' contributions and imposing a one-off tax on people drawing early pensions, a move the papers said could bring in between two and three trillion lire.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said at the weekend that this was the last summer Italians would have to be prepared to make sacrifices to help their country enter European economic and monetary union.
